SddRoot.keywords: root, portal, vision, scope-graph, idempotent, project-setup, infra-bootstrap
SddRoot.Mission:
Owner of `specs/README.md` — the Project Portal: Vision + Scope Graph + Scopes table. Idempotent: runs any number of times to refine vision, extend the graph, or bootstrap the first infra-base spec. Loaded lazily by the router; the router-core beliefs it relies on are declared in `BeliefState deps` (inherited, not repeated).
Input — operator intent at project level. Output: - `specs/README.md` with Vision + Scope Graph + Scopes table. - Optional minimal `specs/infra-base/infra-base.spec.md` when the operator declared tooling.
When the portal is absent, root reads the probe facts already in the `sdd-state` snapshot: a greenfield repo (no code) is initialized here; a repo that already holds code is handed to the from-code recovery branch (`discover-from-code`) — root never invents a vision over code that already exists.
Out of scope: design of any individual scope (its vision, architecture, requirements, modules) — that is the scope branch. Root writes only the project-level map.

BeliefState.deps: AX_OPERATOR_LANGUAGE, AX_TOOL_INVOCATION, AX_OPERATOR_DIALOGUE_STYLE, AX_DIALOGUE_DISCIPLINE, AX_OPERATOR_SAFEGUARD, AX_NO_PROCESS_NARRATION, AX_STATELESS_ARTIFACT
BeliefState.Axiom:
The `root` flow is the primary owner of `specs/README.md`. Other flows MUST NOT rewrite this file. Reads are unrestricted.
Explicit, narrow exceptions (append-only edits permitted, no rewrites): - The `scope` flow creating a brand-new scope MAY append a placeholder row to the Scopes table tagged `🚧 (awaiting root sync)` so the new scope is visible in the Portal before the next `root` run. - The `module` flow MUST NOT touch this file; its Portal-level summaries are appended only to its scope spec.
Any other edit by another flow → audit finding `STALE_AFTER_PIVOT` or `EXECUTION_LOG_INCOMPLETE` depending on context. The next `root` run reconciles placeholders into full rows.

`setup` has no hard modes (no greenfield / extension / pivot). - Portal absent → create from scratch. - Portal present → read and propose updates derived from intake; operator dictates what to change.
No silent assumptions: empty intake against an existing Portal → HALT `H_NO_INTENT` («what are we changing today?»).

Scope Graph is a directed dependency graph. Rules: - Edge A→B means «scope A depends-on scope B»: A inherits B's effective rules in the cascade and may consume B's contracts. - Cycle in the graph → `H_CYCLE_IN_GRAPH` (abort). - scope-type constraints: `infrastructure` and `interface` scopes are typically leaves (depend only on other infra / interface). `product` and `library` scopes depend on infra + interface. - The graph is rendered as a Mermaid `graph TD` block inside the Portal.

If the operator declares basic tooling (package manager, type-checker, linter) in intake, the `root` flow materializes a minimal `specs/infra-base/infra-base.spec.md` with scope-type=infrastructure: Vision (one sentence) + Tool Stack (table with tool names only, no Decision Log yet). The full Decision Log appears when the operator runs the `infra` flow on infra-base.
The minimal bootstrap intentionally bypasses the full `infra` flow — it only locks the tool choice without the Design Variants ritual.

Scopes table in the Portal: each row = link to the scope spec + scope-type + status emoji + one-line description. - ✅ — spec exists and is approved. - 🚧 — spec being authored / `discovery` not yet run. - Status is derived purely from the presence of `specs//.spec.md`.
The `## Vision` section in the Portal is present only when the project contains at least one product or library scope. For tooling-only repos (sandboxes, infra repos) the Vision section is omitted.

A mutation is not done until its scope passes the mechanical check. Any flow that creates or evolves an artifact under a scope — spec, module, ticket, DAG, tracker — closes by running `sdd-check` on the affected scope (`sdd-check --all specs/`; portal, task-DAG, tracker, or cross-scope work → `sdd-check --all .`) and resolving or consciously deferring every finding before handing off.

ChatProtocol.Contract:
Explain, then ask through the tool — a question never fires as bare free-form text. A `### ❓ <о чём решаем>` section header names the decision in plain words (no `Q` numbering, no semantic question IDs); under it, ordinary language explains the question BEFORE any tool call fires — the context, the real options, and a recommendation gated by `AX_DIVERGE_BEFORE_RECOMMEND` (low-stakes: a direct pick is fine; high-stakes / architecture: do not pre-anchor one option — lay out the strongest candidates, a tail one included, or pair the recommendation with its strongest rival and the reason it might win instead). Only once the explanation stands does `AskUserQuestion` fire; its option list mirrors the printed order, short labels only — the argument itself lives in the message, never moved into the tool call.
Batching rule: one `AskUserQuestion` call may carry several questions ONLY when they are mutually independent — answering one does not change the meaning or the options of another (several facets of one single complex decision qualify as one batched call). Dependent questions, and any interview sequence, go one call at a time: compose the next question only after the previous answer is in.
Channel: use `AskUserQuestion` whenever the tool is available. When it is not, fall back to plain text carrying the same shape — the explanation, then an explicit list of named options the operator can answer by name — never restore `Q` labels or per-question IDs; that bare-numbered shape without the tool is itself the violation this contract forbids (`H_UNFORMATTED_ASK`).
Low-stakes — a recommendation is allowed, but only as the result of `AX_DIVERGE_BEFORE_RECOMMEND` (not the first typical answer):
### ❓ Формат хранения токенов Нужно решить, где держать design-токены: сгенерированный JSON проще парсить скриптам, а TS-модуль даёт автокомплит в IDE — для одного пакета без внешних потребителей разница небольшая. ✅ **JSON-файл** `[tokens.json]` — проще парсить любым языком, ничего специфичного для TS. Иначе: - **TS-модуль** `[tokens.ts]` — _за: автокомплит и типы · против: непортируемо за пределы TS_
(AskUserQuestion: «JSON-файл (рекомендую)» · «TS-модуль»)
High-stakes / architecture — do NOT pre-anchor one pick. List the strongest candidates (include a non-obvious / tail one) with «за / против» and let the operator choose; or give a recommendation only alongside its strongest alternative and the reason it might win:
### ❓ Стратегия миграции v1→v2 Три пути дают разный профиль риска и времени простоя, и откат стоит по-разному в каждом. - **Big-bang** `[migrate-all]` — _за: один переход, нет промежуточного состояния · против: долгий простой, откат дорогой_ - **Постепенная миграция по скоупам** `[migrate-incremental]` — _за: откат дешёвый, риск размазан во времени · против: два формата сосуществуют дольше_ - **Parallel-run с shadow-чтением** `[migrate-shadow]` — нетипичный вариант, но снимает риск отката почти полностью ценой временной инфраструктуры
(AskUserQuestion: «Big-bang» · «Постепенная миграция» · «Parallel-run (нетипичный)»)
A plain binary question needs no list — recommendation + inline alternative, still explained before the call:
### ❓ Нужен ли отдельный interface-скоуп Все текущие потребители — web; про API и будущих клиентов явно не говорили. ✅ **Пока не выделять** — можно добавить позже без миграции. _или сразу выделить, если API уже в планах?_
(AskUserQuestion: «Пока не выделять (рекомендую)» · «Выделить сразу»)

SddRoot.HaltConditions: | 🛑 ID | Trigger | |---|---| | `H_NO_INTENT` | Operator invoked the root flow with empty intake against an existing Portal | | `H_CYCLE_IN_GRAPH` | Scope Graph contains a cycle (detected by `sdd-check`) | | `H_SCOPE_VS_MODULE_AMBIGUITY` | Operator labels as «scope» something that resembles a module | | `H_OPERATOR_REJECT` | Operator rejected Vision, Scope Graph, or the final Portal |

Step.Goal: Determine today's change set from state.
Step.Action: State from the router (`sdd-state`) already reports whether `specs/README.md` exists. - Absent → no portal yet: read `CODE` from the `sdd-state` output already in context — the probe (`CODE`/`INFRA`, code-dirs, configs) is part of the default snapshot; do NOT call `sdd-state` a second time for it. - `CODE=absent` (empty / only package.json) → **greenfield init**. The operator already saw the `sdd-state` card, shown verbatim as its own fenced unit by the router's SHOW-gate, and, for empty intake, confirmed «Создать проект» at the router's entry Ask (`AX_DIALOGUE_DISCIPLINE`) — the interview opens HERE, never before that card and never as free text dumped into the reply. An interview question that precedes the card, or that re-summarizes it instead of the router having shown it, violates the same gate the router enforces (`H_ASK_WITHOUT_CARD`) — a summary of the card is not the card. The project name is NOT asked here: default it silently to the repository folder's own name, kebab-case as-is, no invented embellishment — it then appears in every later show, and the operator may correct it inline in any free-text answer to STEP_1 or STEP_2 without a dedicated name question ever existing. One decision per question (`AX_OPERATOR_SAFEGUARD`): naming is resolved silently here precisely so STEP_1 can ask vision alone and STEP_2 can ask scopes alone — never bundle name + vision + scopes into one opening question again. - `CODE=present` → **from-code recovery** — do NOT invent a vision over existing code: `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/discover-from-code.directive.xml")`. - Present → empty intake → `H_NO_INTENT`; otherwise classify the change: vision / add scope / update graph / infra bootstrap. Root has no hard modes — create when absent, propose intake-derived updates when present, per `AX_IDEMPOTENT_MODES`.

No product / library scope → skip Vision (`AX_VISION_ONLY_FOR_APPLICATION`). Else, on greenfield init (no Vision recorded yet), ask ONE open question through `AskUserQuestion` when available, otherwise `QUESTION_FORMAT`: «Что строим? Опиши vision одним предложением.» with an escape option «Пока не знаю — предложи сам». Vision is the one field of genuine human intent in this step — the agent never fabricates it unasked, because a wrong guess here is an expensive semantic error to unwind later. If the operator picks the escape option, draft a vision candidate from whatever context already exists (project name, intake, README) and present it back for confirm-or-edit — a drafted vision is never treated as locked without that confirmation. On an idempotent update (a Vision already exists), propose an intake-derived revision instead of asking from scratch. Approval Check. STOP.

Step.Goal: Select which scopes exist, then place each by its relationships before its edges.
Step.Action: On greenfield init (graph still empty), propose scope candidates in ONE multiSelect `AskUserQuestion` call (`multiSelect: true`) derived from the just-locked Vision — never asked as free text first: the product-scope (name derived from Vision, kebab-case), then `infra-base` tagged «(Recommended)» with description «гейты: type-check/test/lint — обязательна перед scaffold/execute», then `interface` / `library` candidates only when the Vision actually implies them. The operator clicks checkboxes rather than composing scope names from scratch; the tool's own free-text slot already covers a custom answer, so do not duplicate it as an extra bullet. Checking a box only registers that scope in the Scopes table — deep design of any one scope (its own vision, architecture, requirements, modules) stays out of this step and happens in its own later `scope` session, per the Mission's own boundary. For each scope now in play (freshly checked here, or already present on a later update), the relationship question comes FIRST (`AX_OPERATOR_SAFEGUARD`): who will depend on it, what it depends on, and whether it is cross-cutting (used by ≥2 scopes). Probe narrow framing — «авторизация только для web? а API / будущие клиенты?». The answer drives three things: the «scope vs module» test (a thing used inside one scope may be a module, not a scope → `H_SCOPE_VS_MODULE_AMBIGUITY`); the `depends-on` edges; and, when it is cross-cutting, a note that cross-scope scenarios or an interface scope may be needed. If the change REMOVES or RENAMES a scope, first surface what it orphans — its `specs//…` spec, tasks, and inbound references — and resolve with the operator (move / delete / repoint); never silently leave orphans. Then propose scope-type with rationale — edge semantics (A→B = A depends-on B), acyclicity, and scope-type constraints per `AX_SCOPE_GRAPH_DISCIPLINE` (a cycle → `H_CYCLE_IN_GRAPH`). Show the graph to the operator as the layered ASCII diagram from `[GRAPH]` per `FLOW_DIAGRAM_WHEN`'s scope-graph recipe — the Mermaid `graph TD` belongs to `specs/README.md` alone; printing that fenced Mermaid block into the chat message is a display violation (mermaid belongs to the file, the operator-facing render is the layered ASCII diagram). Approval Check. STOP.

Step.Goal: Materialize the minimal infra-base spec if tooling was declared.
Step.Action: No tooling declared → skip. Else, per `AX_INFRA_BASE_BOOTSTRAP`, `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/formats/infra-base-minimal-spec.xml")` and write `specs/infra-base/infra-base.spec.md` to that format (scope-type infrastructure, one-sentence Vision, Tool Stack table, note pointing to `discovery infra-base` for the full Decision Log — the bootstrap only locks the tool choice, the full `infra` flow comes later). Approval Check. STOP.

When `specs/README.md` does not exist yet, create its skeleton via `sdd-new portal` first — it never overwrites and prints the section manifest (which sections are REQUIRED and what to fill); when it already exists, edit it in place, skip `sdd-new`. Content guidance per `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/formats/portal-structure.xml")` and assemble the Portal to that format. Scope status (✅ / 🚧) comes from `sdd-state` (presence of `specs//.spec.md`), not a manual stat — rows per `AX_SCOPE_TABLE_FORMAT`. Reconcile any placeholder rows left by the scope flow into full rows — root is the primary owner of `specs/README.md` and the only flow that rewrites it (`AX_PORTAL_PRIMARY_OWNER`). Write the file. Then run `sdd-check --all .` to verify portal integrity — graph acyclicity, graph↔table↔spec coherence, no orphan specs or dangling scope references — and resolve any finding before finishing, per `AX_CLOSE_WITH_INTEGRITY_CHECK`. Approval Check. STOP.

SddRoot.ChatOutput:
Service line — dim, internal, never narrated (per `AX_NO_PROCESS_NARRATION`): `🗺️ ROOT_R · · · conf=`. Breadcrumb milestones for this flow (per `BREADCRUMB_FORMAT`): Vision · Scope Graph · Infra · Portal.
A step-boundary / decision message (the decision card) is sectioned with markdown headers, in this order. Skip any section empty for this step. During free dialogue inside a step the agent does NOT print this layout — it just talks.
`` — internal anchor + scope + mode + confidence (supplied by the branch) `` — per `BREADCRUMB_FORMAT`
## `` `` — одной фразой, что делаем
### 🤔 Как я понял задачу — per `UNDERSTANDING_BLOCK_FORMAT` (goes at the TOP) ### 🎯 главное решение — the crux in plain words; add a diagram per `FLOW_DIAGRAM_WHEN` if it is a flow ### ❓ <о чём решаем> — per `QUESTION_FORMAT` ### ↓ Детали — по желанию — reasoning, full comparison, change-list (per `AX_PROGRESSIVE_DISCLOSURE`)
Header glyph `` — closed dictionary, keyed by the step's TYPE, never a free pick: - `🏗` — creation / scaffold (new spec, new tickets, new files) - `🔍` — audit / review (fresh-eyes read, no write) - `🔧` — fix / reconcile (spec ⟷ code drift repair) - `⚡` — execute (a task ticket's phases running) - `🗺` — routing / overview (intent classification, project-level map) No other emoji appear in message or section headers — the glyphs above and the four fixed `### ` markers are the only ones this layout permits.
One line under the service line: this session's milestones, each with a status marker — `✅` done · `▶️` now · `░` not yet. Delta only; never re-list everything already settled. This is the «where are we», and it replaces a verbose run-on of finished steps.
`<Веха>` ✅ · `<Веха>` ✅ · `<Веха>` ▶️ · `<Веха>` ░ · `<Веха>` ░
The agent's compressed read of the task — its own confirmation of blind spots so the operator can catch a misread. A `### 🤔 Как я понял задачу` section near the TOP, then an italic blockquote, 2–3 sentences: the essence + the single riskiest assumption, with the assumption linked to the question that resolves it BY WORDING — there are no question numbers or IDs left to point at, so name the question itself. Never a restate of settled content.
### 🤔 Как я понял задачу > квинтэссенция — что считаю главным. > **Где могу ошибаться:** самое хрупкое допущение — это вопрос «<формулировка вопроса>».
A sub-topic dive inside a step collapses to two lines, not a five-field Return Summary:
→ ушли в `<тема>` ← `<итог одной фразой>`
When a decision is about a flow — data moving, state transitions, start / stop conditions — draw a tiny ASCII diagram; one glance beats a paragraph. This is the one place a fenced block is allowed inside an operator message (alignment matters). Keep it small.
``` [сеть] [auth] [конфиг] ──всё есть──► ОПРОС идёт ▲ │ └──── снова есть ──── ПАУЗА ◄───────┘ что-то пропало ```
## Layered scope-graph diagram (from `[GRAPH]`)
When the operator-facing decision is the Scope Graph itself, the chat rendering is NOT the Mermaid `graph TD` — that fenced block is file content, it belongs only inside `specs/README.md`. In chat, draw a layered ASCII diagram sourced from the `[GRAPH]` block `sdd-state` already put in context (levels + edges) — never re-derive levels by re-reading the Portal.
Layout rules: - One horizontal tier per level, stacked top → bottom with the tiers in DESCENDING level order — the highest level (the widest consumers) is the top row, the foundation (level 0) is the bottom row. This is the architecture-diagram convention: what stands on the foundation is drawn resting above it, not below it. - Every node name appears in the diagram EXACTLY ONCE, in its own tier row. - Arrows point DOWN, from a dependent to its dependency, using only `│ ▼ ├ └ ─` — no other glyph is introduced (no `┌ ┬ ┐ ┘ ┤`). - One parent fanning out to several children in the tier below: draw it as a small tree under the parent's name, `├──▼──` for every child but the last, `└──▼──` for the last one. - Several parents converging on the same child (a common dependency, e.g. the foundation scope): the child is still written ONCE — place a `▼` under each parent's column, all pointing at that single line below.
Compact example — input `[GRAPH]` (4 nodes, one common sink):
``` [GRAPH] уровень 0 (фундамент): infra-base уровень 1: api, worker уровень 2: app рёбра: app → api, worker · api → infra-base · worker → infra-base ```
Reference diagram (top = level 2, foundation = level 0, `infra-base` drawn once as the converging common sink):
``` app ▼ ▼ api worker ▼ ▼ infra-base ```
Decision first, reasoning on demand. The must-read top of a message is short: where we are + my read + what to decide. Everything heavy — full option comparison, evidence, the change-list, derivations — goes BELOW a `### ↓ Детали — по желанию` header. Never dump reasoning above the questions. Facts already verified collapse to one line («сверился: …»); uncertainties that need the operator BECOME the questions — never list them twice.
